messages.content: Why do we only use 10% of our brains?

response.text:
The idea that we only use 10% of our brains is a myth and has been debunked by neuroscientists. Brain imaging studies show that we use virtually all parts of our brain, and each region has a known function. While it is true that not all neurons are firing at the same time, and some areas may be more active during specific tasks, the entire brain is involved in various functions throughout the day.

The misconception may have originated from misinterpretations of neurological research or from the way people understand brain function. In reality, the brain is a highly efficient organ, and even when we are at rest, many areas are still active, maintaining essential functions such as regulating bodily processes and processing information.

In summary, we use much more than just 10% of our brains; the entire organ is engaged in a wide range of activities, both conscious and unconscious.
